title: Taiwanese Inventors Win 50 Medals at German Invention Fair
summaryZh: 台灣在德國iENA發明展奪50面獎牌，台東學生智慧背心等獲金牌。
summaryHi: जर्मनी के iENA आविष्कार मेले में ताइवान ने 50 पदक जीते; ताइतुंग के छात्रों की स्मार्ट जैकेट को स्वर्ण।
summaryEs: Taiwán gana 50 medallas en la feria de inventos iENA de Alemania; un chaleco inteligente escolar logra oro.
summaryJa: 台湾がドイツのiENA発明展でメダル50個、台東の中学生のスマートベストが金賞。
summaryKo: 대만, 독일 iENA 발명전에서 메달 50개… 타이둥 학생들의 스마트 조끼 금상.
summaryEn: Taiwan won 50 medals at Germany’s iENA invention fair, with students’ smart bike vest among the golds.
paragraphs: Taiwan has brought home 50 medals from the 2026 iENA invention fair in Germany, winning 12 golds, 15 silvers and 23 bronzes, according to the Taiwan Invention Association (TIA), which led a 78-member delegation to the event.
Held in Nuremberg from 31 October to 2 November, the fair featured 580 inventions presented by 340 exhibitors from 21 countries and regions, the event's official website said.

Some of the most eye-catching entries came from schools in Taitung County. Students at Feng-tian Junior High School won gold for a smart safety vest for cyclists. Its lights signal which way the rider intends to turn, triggered either by a wireless button on the handlebars or automatically through Google Maps, and it flashes red when the rider brakes at night.

Another gold went to a Tung Hai Junior High School student for a multifunctional nail-trimming box fitted with a magnifying glass, which analyses nails and clippings to offer personalised health suggestions. Students at St Joseph Technical Senior High School were also honoured for a height-adjustable urinal that uses infrared sensors to fit each user and reduce splashing in public restrooms.

Taiwanese care brand O'right took gold for a shampoo designed for greying hair. TIA chairwoman Chang Chia-chu said education should go beyond passing on knowledge and instead cultivate independent thinking, innovation and practical problem-solving.
Taiwan did very well at a big invention fair in Germany. Its inventors won 50 medals: 12 gold, 15 silver and 23 bronze.
The fair, called iENA, was in the city of Nuremberg from 31 October to 2 November. There were 580 inventions from 21 countries and regions. The Taiwan Invention Association took 78 inventors there.
Some winners were young students from Taitung. One group made a smart vest for people on bikes. Its lights show when the rider will turn left or right. At night, it flashes red when the rider stops.

Another student made a box for cutting nails. It has a small glass to make things look bigger. It can also give health tips. Older students made a toilet for men that moves up or down to fit the user's height.
A Taiwanese company also won gold for a shampoo for grey hair. The head of the association said school should teach children to think for themselves and solve real problems.

共有來自21個國家和地區的580件發明。
中華創新發明學會帶了78位發明人前往。
有些得獎者是來自台東的年輕學生。
其中一組做了一件給騎腳踏車的人穿的智慧背心。
它的燈會顯示騎士什麼時候要左轉或右轉。
到了晚上，騎士停下來時，它會閃紅燈。
另一名學生做了一個剪指甲用的盒子。
它有一片小鏡片，能讓東西看起來更大。
它也能提供健康小建議。
年紀較大的學生做了一個男用小便斗，能上下移動來配合使用者的身高。
一家台灣公司也以一款白髮專用洗髮精贏得金牌。
學會的負責人說，學校應該教孩子獨立思考、解決真實的問題。

paragraphs: Taiwanese inventors returned from a major invention fair in Germany with 50 medals, including 12 golds, 15 silvers and 23 bronzes, the Taiwan Invention Association (TIA) said.

The 2026 iENA fair took place in Nuremberg from 31 October to 2 November. According to the event's website, 340 exhibitors from 21 countries and regions showed 580 inventions there. The TIA led a team of 78 Taiwanese inventors.

Several gold medals went to school students from Taitung County. Pupils from Feng-tian Junior High School designed a smart safety vest for cyclists. Its lights show which way the rider is going to turn, using a button on the handlebars or a link to Google Maps. At night, it also flashes red when the rider brakes.

A student from Tung Hai Junior High School made a nail-cutting box with a magnifying glass that studies nails and gives health advice. Students from St Joseph Technical Senior High School built a urinal that uses sensors to change its height for each user, which helps keep public toilets cleaner.
The care brand O'right also won gold for a shampoo for grey hair. TIA chairwoman Chang Chia-chu said education should teach young people to think independently and solve practical problems.

paragraphs: Taiwanese inventors have returned from Germany with a haul of 50 medals from the 2026 iENA international invention fair, comprising 12 golds, 15 silvers and 23 bronzes, the Taiwan Invention Association (TIA) has announced.
The fair, staged in Nuremberg from 31 October to 2 November, showcased 580 inventions from 340 exhibitors representing 21 countries and regions. The TIA headed a delegation of 78 Taiwanese inventors.

Notably, several of the top awards went to schoolchildren from Taitung County. A team from Feng-tian Junior High School earned gold for a smart safety vest that lets cyclists indicate an upcoming turn, activated either by a wireless handlebar button or automatically via Google Maps integration, while a flashing red light warns drivers when the rider brakes after dark.

A pupil from Tung Hai Junior High School was recognised for a multifunctional nail-trimming box equipped with a magnifier that analyses nails and clippings to generate tailored health advice. Meanwhile, students from St Joseph Technical Senior High School devised a height-adjustable urinal whose infrared sensors gauge the user's height, with a retractable drainage pipe designed to curb splashing and improve hygiene.

On the commercial side, the care brand O'right secured gold for a caffeine-based shampoo aimed at greying hair. Reflecting on the results, TIA chairwoman Chang Chia-chu argued that education ought to foster independent thinking and real-world problem-solving rather than merely transmitting knowledge.
sentZh: 中華創新發明學會（TIA）宣布，台灣發明人從德國2026年iENA國際發明展滿載而歸，共奪得50面獎牌，包括12金、15銀和23銅。
這場於10月31日至11月2日在紐倫堡舉辦的發明展，展示了代表21個國家和地區的340個參展者所帶來的580件發明。
TIA率領了一支由78位台灣發明人組成的代表團。
值得注意的是，好幾項大獎由台東縣的學童拿下。
豐田國中的團隊以一件智慧安全背心贏得金牌，它讓騎士能預先示意即將轉彎，可透過車把上的無線按鈕或整合Google地圖自動啟動，天黑後騎士煞車時，閃爍的紅燈也會提醒駕駛人。
東海國中一名學生以一款多功能修剪指甲盒獲得肯定，它配備放大鏡，能分析指甲和指甲屑，產生量身打造的健康建議。
與此同時，聖若瑟高職的學生設計出一款可調高度的小便斗，以紅外線感應器偵測使用者身高，並搭配可伸縮的排水管，以減少噴濺、改善衛生。
在商業方面，保養品牌歐萊德以一款針對白髮、以咖啡因為基底的洗髮精奪得金牌。
談到這次的成績，TIA理事長張家菊主張，教育應該培養獨立思考和解決現實問題的能力，而不只是傳遞知識。

paragraphs: It is often said that necessity is the mother of invention. For a group of Taiwanese teenagers, everyday challenges such as staying safe on a bike or keeping public toilets clean became the focus of award-winning designs at the 2026 iENA invention fair in Nuremberg, Germany.

Taiwan's 78-strong delegation, organised by the Taiwan Invention Association (TIA), collected 50 medals in total, namely 12 golds, 15 silvers and 23 bronzes. The competition, held from 31 October to 2 November, attracted 580 inventions from 340 exhibitors across 21 countries and regions.

Among the standout entries was a smart safety vest developed by pupils at Feng-tian Junior High School in Taitung, which signals a cyclist's intended turn through a wireless handlebar button or Google Maps integration and flashes red when the rider brakes at night. Other Taitung schools also struck gold: one student designed a nail-trimming box that analyses clippings to offer health recommendations, while a senior high school team engineered a height-adjustable urinal with infrared sensors to minimise splashing.

Commercial innovation featured too, with the care brand O'right winning gold for a shampoo formulated for greying hair without five potentially harmful ingredients that the TIA says are common in hair dyes.

For TIA chairwoman Chang Chia-chu, the results carry a broader lesson. In her view, education should not be confined to the transfer of knowledge but should nurture independent thought and the capacity to tackle practical problems.
sentZh: 俗話說，需要是發明之母。
對一群台灣青少年來說，騎車安全、保持公廁清潔這類日常難題，成了他們在德國紐倫堡2026年iENA發明展上得獎設計的焦點。
由中華創新發明學會（TIA）組織的78人台灣代表團，總共拿下50面獎牌，即12金、15銀和23銅。
這項於10月31日至11月2日舉行的比賽，吸引了來自21個國家和地區、340個參展者的580件發明。
其中一件出色的作品是台東豐田國中學生開發的智慧安全背心，它能透過車把上的無線按鈕或整合Google地圖，示意騎士打算轉彎的方向，並在夜間騎士煞車時閃紅燈。
其他台東學校也奪得金牌：一名學生設計了能分析指甲屑並提供健康建議的修剪指甲盒，而一支高中團隊則打造了配備紅外線感應器、可調高度的小便斗，以盡量減少噴濺。
商業創新也有亮眼表現，保養品牌歐萊德以一款白髮專用洗髮精奪金，該產品不含TIA所說染髮劑中常見的五種潛在有害成分。
對TIA理事長張家菊而言，這些成果帶來更廣泛的啟示。
她認為，教育不應侷限於知識的傳遞，而應培養獨立思考及處理實際問題的能力。
